contract: CBWeb3 Scenario B — Hub-and-spoke settlement (reserve lifecycle)

vectors.title: Register a fiat deposit on a Scenario B spoke
vectors.description: Step 1 of the mandatory reserve prelude. Without tCeBM on its own spoke a bank cannot be bridged into the Hub and cannot pay.

preconditions.session: access_token cookie for a commercial-bank participant

vectors.notes: Scenario B's request has no requester_paladin_identity field at all, unlike Scenario A's. requester_besu_address is scoped to the verified caller by the relay and is overwritten if sent. Amounts on the /api/v1 surface are 7-digit-looking opaque strings with no stated unit; amounts on /api/v2 are explicitly 18-decimal base units. There is no documented conversion between the two, so never move a figure from a deposit straight into a swap.

vectors.title: Central Bank approves the deposit
vectors.description: Moves the record to APPROVED. As in Scenario A the platform answers 201 rather than 200.

vectors.title: Fiat exchange at .../deposits/exchange, not .../deposits/fiat-exchange
vectors.description: The Scenario B path and response field both differ from Scenario A. Neither gateway serves the other's path, so this is the single most likely place a client written for one scenario silently 404s against the other.
vectors.notes: Scenario A returns tx_hash here; Scenario B returns mint_tx_hash. The platform's own summary and field description for this operation say the token minted is tCeBM. Both are wrong: the token minted is fCeBM, the ERC-20 fiat token. tCeBM appears one step later, at escrows/approve.

vectors.title: Request Reserve Tokenisation, quoting the approved deposit
vectors.description: Scenario B's escrow request carries an extra deposit_id linking the tokenisation to the deposit that funded it. Scenario A's does not.
vectors.notes: The platform's own description of amount on this request reads 'tCeBM to convert into tCeBM'. The real conversion is fCeBM to tCeBM.

vectors.title: Approve the escrow — burn fCeBM, mint tCeBM
vectors.description: Two chains move. Note the second hash is mint_tx_hash here, where Scenario A calls the same value zeto_mint_tx_hash.

vectors.title: tCeBM balance is non-zero — the gate on every swap
vectors.description: The reserve prelude is not optional in Scenario B: bridge lock-mint locks spoke tCeBM the bank must already hold, and a cross-currency swap bridges in on the payer's behalf.
vectors.notes: Capture this value before a swap and compare after: the payer must be debited amount_in, NOT max_amount_in. See amm_swap_vectors.json swap-hp-04.

vectors.title: List escrows scoped to the calling bank
vectors.description: No pagination. On a commercial-bank gateway the relay pins the scope to the caller regardless of the requester_id sent.
vectors.notes: Scenario B's escrow records carry besu_address where Scenario A's carry requester_besu_address, plus an extra requester_id bank code. The two record shapes are not interchangeable.

vectors.title: Escrow amount sent as a JSON number is 400
vectors.description: Amounts are decimal strings everywhere on this surface. A JSON number fails body parsing.
vectors.notes: 400 is declared on this operation. A body that parses but omits amount is refused further downstream; the reserve handlers do not translate that failure into a 400, so expect 500 there rather than 400.

vectors.title: Approving an escrow without the Central Bank role is 403
vectors.description: Every Central-Bank-side reserve mutation in Scenario B is role-gated exactly as in Scenario A.

preconditions.session: valid cookie WITHOUT the central_bank role

vectors.notes: The role in the token is the lowercase Keycloak realm role central_bank. ROLE_CENTRAL_BANK_SCENARIO_B, which the platform document writes in prose, is a Go constant name and never appears in a JWT.

vectors.title: No session cookie is 401 on the fiat balance probe
vectors.description: Confirms the /api/v1 surface in Scenario B is cookie-guarded too. Bearer tokens are accepted only on twelve /api/v2 routes and on none of these.

vectors.title: A gateway with no fiat adapter answers 503, not 500
vectors.description: getFiatBalance is the only operation in either scenario that declares a 503. It is a deployment-shape signal — this node has no fiat token adapter wired — and not a transient fault to retry.

preconditions.gateway: a deployment with no fiat token adapter configured

vectors.notes: A conformance runner should SKIP rather than FAIL when a gateway profile lacks the adapter. The same reasoning applies to a 404 from a route group the deployment never registered, and to the 501 on GET /api/v2/amm/swap/cross-currency when no history reader is wired.
